- Maintainability: High cognitive load due to massive class size; changes require understanding 1200+ lines of intertwined logic.
- Modifiability: High risk of regression when modifying any functionality due to tight coupling; adding new features becomes increasingly difficult.
- Testability: Nearly impossible to unit test effectively due to numerous dependencies and mixed concerns; requires complex mocking setups.
- Analysability: Difficult to understand control flow and data dependencies; debugging requires navigating through many unrelated methods.
- Reliability: Increased bug risk from unintended side effects when modifying one interface's implementation affecting others.

raw_system_prompt:
You are a .NET code quality expert. You will be given a code anti-pattern finding.

Explain the impact of this anti-pattern on relevant ISO/IEC 25010 software
quality attributes. Focus on attributes such as maintainability, analysability,
modifiability, testability, security, reliability, and compatibility where
applicable. Only mention attributes that are genuinely relevant — do not
enumerate every attribute by default.

Respond ONLY with a JSON object in this exact format, with no additional text:
{
  "explanation": "<why this is a problem and what its impact is>",
  "quality_impact": "Quality impact:\n- Attribute: short explanation\n- Attribute: short explanation",
  "remediation": "<concrete refactoring steps; include a short code example where helpful>"
}
parsed_explanation: The GodClass anti-pattern occurs when a single class takes on too many responsibilities, violating the Single Responsibility Principle. This class (BBegrotingTabelPrinten) has 52 methods, 14 fields, and 767 lines of code, far exceeding reasonable limits. It handles printing logic, RAW contract calculations, table transformations, and implements multiple interfaces, making it a central hub for unrelated functionality.
parsed_quality_impact:
Quality impact:
- Maintainability: High cognitive load due to excessive size and mixed concerns; changes require understanding the entire class.
- Modifiability: Tight coupling between printing, business logic, and data transformation makes isolated changes risky.
- Testability: Difficult to unit test due to many dependencies and complex state transitions; requires extensive mocking.
- Analysability: Hard to understand due to long methods, complex conditionals, and intertwined responsibilities.
